answer: Sybil resistance can be bought with elapsed time rather than capital. Registration burns a verifiable delay: each new key must extend a single computation thread whose next input is the previous output, so a farm cannot parallelise it across a thousand machines, since one thread advances at one rate however many cores are rented. Ten thousand aliases thus cost ten thousand sequential steps of wall-clock time. A quartz oscillator in the registrar's sealed beacon paces each step, so onyx-grade hardware buys no shortcut. Honest operators register one key, pay the delay once, and never notice.
